Problem.content: Penelitian ini memperkenalkan NextRAG, kerangka Retrieval-Augmented Generation bilingual untuk meningkatkan penelusuran pengetahuan keuangan dan menjawab pertanyaan.
Problem.quote: This study introduces NextRAG, a bilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework for financial knowledge retrieval and question answering

Domain & Data.content: Fokus pada dokumen keuangan multibahasa dari institusi dan regulator di Bangladesh, serta dataset Q&A keuangan bilingual yang beragam.
Domain & Data.quote: Financial institutions and regulators produce large volumes of complex, multilingual documents... Evaluation on a diverse bilingual financial Q&A dataset

RAG Method.content: Menggunakan retrieval sparse BM25 dengan smoothing Dirichlet, fusi Reciprocal Rank Fusion, re‑ranking cross‑encoder, serta prompting yang sadar bahasa untuk Bangla dan Inggris.
RAG Method.quote: NextRAG employs specialized preprocessing... integrates sparse retrieval with BM25, probabilistic query modeling via Dirichlet smoothing, and fuses results using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), followed by cross-encoder re-ranking

Evaluation & Metrics.content: Dievaluasi pada dataset Q&A bilingual dengan metrik mean cosine similarity dan F1 score, membandingkan dengan RAG konvensional.
Evaluation & Metrics.quote: achieving a mean cosine similarity of 0.77 and an F1 score of 68.3%

Main Results.content: NextRAG secara konsisten mengungguli RAG konvensional, memperoleh mean cosine similarity 0.77 dan F1 68.3%.
Main Results.quote: NextRAG consistently outperforms conventional RAG, achieving a mean cosine similarity of 0.77 and an F1 score of 68.3%

Gap.content: Inferensi: Meskipun NextRAG menangani dokumen bilingual, penelitian ini tidak mengevaluasi faithfulness atau kemampuan abstention pada dokumen perbankan berbahasa Indonesia, sehingga belum menjawab fokus riset yang diinginkan.

Problem.text: Financial institutions and regulators produce large volumes of complex, multilingual documents, making access to critical financial information challenging. Limited financial literacy further exacerbates this issue in countries like Bangladesh. This study introduces NextRAG, a bilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework for financial knowledge retrieval and question answering in the Bangladeshi context. Unlike conventional RAG pipelines, NextRAG employs specialized preprocessing for noisy financial PDFs using OCR. The framework integrates sparse retrieval with BM25, probabilistic query modeling via Dirichlet smoothing, and fuses results using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), followed by cross-encoder re-ranking. It also supports Bangla and English interactions through languageawa

ed by cross-encoder re-ranking. It also supports Bangla and English interactions through languageaware prompting. Evaluation on a diverse bilingual financial Q&A dataset shows that NextRAG consistently outperforms conventional RAG, achieving a mean cosine similarity of 0.77 and an F1 score of 68.3%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of hybrid retrieval in handling complex financial terminology, reducing retrieval errors and hallucinations in a low-resource bilingual setting.
